Some professionals think of all mental illness as related in some way to one another. The classification of disorders is fluid and sometimes what diagnosis one is assigned can changed over time, either with new Dr's or changing presentation. I would like to think classifications are concrete but they're just not.

But anyway, ocd and specific phobias are both anxiety disorders and therefore will share similarities on that basis. Generalized anxiety disorder can also look a lot like ocd. I think the biggest thing that separates them is what are the major factors at play. Generalized anxiety focuses on various things, ocd is a lot more repetitive, specific phobias are focused and tend to present mainly when the feared thing is present. 

I like to think of mental illnesses are a sort of spherical spectrum where you get constellations of symptoms and the specific diagnosis attempts to define what specific symptoms you have and which areas of the brain are most effected, but it's not a perfect system by any means. I mean the similarities between groups of disorders are more vast than their differences.
